prompt:
Scene:
A square color magazine advertisement page in the style of 1960 American home-appliance print ads. Full product-hero layout: appliance centered in an idealized kitchen corner vignette, top banner area, bottom tagline area. Halftone grain, slight CMYK offset, matte coated paper feel.

Subject:
An imaginary atomic-age wall-mounted auto-pantry: a rounded cabinet in powder-pink enamel set into the wall, with a vertical rotating carousel of small labeled bins visible through a large porthole window. Below the porthole a row of five amber glowing buttons. A chrome dispenser chute at the bottom delivers a single red apple onto a small ivory tray. To the right of the unit stands a stylized mid-century child in a yellow pajama suit reaching for the apple, eyes wide with wonder. Small boomerang wallpaper pattern behind.

Important details:
Strict atomic-age palette: ivory, turquoise, cadmium red, bright yellow, powder pink, chrome. Auto-pantry form must feel like what 1960 imagined future home food storage: rounded edges, chrome trim, big porthole, analog buttons. The bins inside must suggest simple labeled compartments without readable text. Illustration style is halftone print ad, not photo. The child is a stylized cartoon figure.

Use case:
Atomic Appliance Studies single study 2 of 5, independent product ad mockup.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no LCD display, no touchscreen, no photoreal skin, no modern minimalist wall unit, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
